Paragraph: "He is the protector of all beings and the follower of father's directives, he is the eldest one among the sons of King Dasharatha... possessor of high virtues, qualities and royal fortune befitting to a king... but he is deprived of his kingdom, and came hither to dwell in the forests... nevertheless, followed by me...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Explaining the contrast between Rama's royal worth and his current exile.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Explaining obedience to paternal command (pitru-vachana) and uncomplaining acceptance of exile.
Outcome/Resolution: Clarifies the noble reason behind their presence in the forest.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Work-Life Balance: Unwavering commitment to duty over personal comfort

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Pitru-bhakti (devotion and obedience to parental duty)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Rama's adherence to his father's word exemplifies supreme pitru-bhakti and satya-vrata.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Demonstrates value-driven behavior, prioritizing moral integrity over personal ease.
